import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 323

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/323](https://www.erdosproblems.com/323)
-/

open Filter
open scoped Asymptotics

namespace Erdos323

/--
Let $1\leq m\leq k$ and $f_{k,m}(x)$ denote the number of integers $\leq x$ which are the sum of
$m$ many nonnegative $k$th powers.
-/
noncomputable def f (k m x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  { n : ℕ | n ≤ x ∧ ∃ (v : Fin m → ℕ), n = ∑ i, v i ^ k }.ncard

/--
Is it true that $f_{k,k}(x) \gg_\epsilon x^{1-\epsilon}$ for all $\epsilon>0$?

This would have significant applications to Waring's problem. Erdős and Graham describe this as
'unattackable by the methods at our disposal'.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_323.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε)) =O[atTop] (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f k k x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that if $m < k$ then $f_{k,m}(x) \gg x^{m/k}$ for sufficiently large $x$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_323.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → m < k →
      (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ ((m : ℝ) / (k : ℝ))) =O[atTop] (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f k m x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
The case $k=2$ was resolved by Landau, who showed $f_{2,2}(x) \sim \frac{cx}{\sqrt{\log x}}$ for
some constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_323.variants.k_eq_2 :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f 2 2 x : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ c * (x : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log (x : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
For $k>2$ it is not known if $f_{k,k}(x)=o(x)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_323.variants.k_gt_2 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k > 2, (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (f k k x : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos323

reformulations.difference: The original Erdős–Graham formulation on p. 45 asks for the eventual strict bound f_{k,k}(x) > x^(1−ε), with coefficient 1, for every ε > 0. Lean instead uses x^(1−ε) = O(f_{k,k}(x)), allowing an implied constant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Fix k ≥ 1. The unit-coefficient bound immediately implies the Big-O statement. Conversely, apply the Big-O assertion at ε/2 to obtain f_{k,k}(x) ≥ C⁻¹ x^(1−ε/2) eventually, with C > 0. Since x^(ε/2) eventually exceeds C, this gives f_{k,k}(x) > x^(1−ε). The equivalence for each k was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review323.all_epsilon_iff_unit_coefficient, without using any admitted problem theorem.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), §5, pp. 45–46; positive-constant convention on p. 11. https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf (read using OCR of the scanned pages).
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml — entry 323 records the problem as open.

Local Mathlib sources: Data/Set/Card.lean; Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean, Lemmas.lean, and AsymptoticEquivalent.lean; Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean and Asymptotics.lean; Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean; Analysis/Real/Sqrt.lean.
Local repository guidance and machinery: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, and FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes:
All five declarations match the original source. Direct requests to erdosproblems.com/323 returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the mathematical comparison used Erdős–Graham pp. 45–46 instead. The public problem database still records 323 as open; live-page-specific updates could not be inspected directly.

Lean checks established finiteness of every counted set, equivalence with a computable finite enumeration, f(k,m,0)=1 for k>0, and f(1,1,x)=x+1. Small cases included f(2,2,12)=8 and f(3,3,12)=7. Additional proofs verified the lower-bound direction of both Big-O statements, the ratio interpretations of the Landau and little-o variants, positivity of the logarithmic denominator eventually, and harmlessness of the k=1 and ε≥1 cases. The scratch file compiles successfully; the checked equivalences have no sorry dependencies. No repository files were modified.
